text:
cheng li: FYI bringing up aurora-lite-v2 (compact int8) on staging. quick smoke showed odd detok behavior around furigana/ruby and soft hyphens in JP->ZH/KO test sets.

miki tanaka: can you paste an example output + reference?

cheng li: sure — sample src (JP with ruby):
```
彼・　<ruby>学校<rt>がっこう</rt></ruby>へ行った。
```
model output (detok):
- correct: 他去了学校。
- aurora-lite-v2 int8: 他去了学­校。
(note the soft-hyphen inserted in the middle of 学校)

raj patel: soft-hyphen? that smells like printer-friendly hyphenation inserted by detok step. is this only JP->ZH or also JP->EN?

cheng li: jp->en shows token-split: "school" -> "sch­ool" sometimes in streaming responses. also appears in zh/ko outputs when ruby preceded by interpunct.

sasha ivanova: any recent tokenizer/regression CLs? we had a change in the detok normalization last week (strip_invisible=false toggle) for faster streaming.

kevin o'neill: i rolled back that flag in staging a few hours ago, but hadn't run full evals. could be interaction with quantization kernel that emits different token boundaries for furigana tags.

cheng li: repro steps i used:
```bash
# run single-shot eval on test subset
python evals/run.py --model aurora-lite-v2 --quant int8 --subset jp_furigana_short --detok-engine fast-detok-v2
```
metrics: jp->zh BLEU drop -3.1 vs fp16 baseline on the subset, precision on punctuation messed.

eval-bot: ci/evals/aurora-lite-v2/int8/678 finished — avg BLEU delta: JP->ZH -3.12, JP->EN -1.8, ZH->EN -0.2. Examples flagged: 12/200 have embedded U+00AD or ZWSP in detok.

miki tanaka: interesting — how many of those examples include ruby/furigana tags in the source vs being added by preprocessing?

cheng li: about 9 of 12 have explicit <ruby> in the HTML->text pipeline. the rest are mixed-width punctuation with U+30FB interpunct preceding ruby.

raj patel: could be kv-cache alignment changes under int8 quant that shift subtoken merges. Did you compare tokenization (pre-quant) vs model token boundaries?

cheng li: yes — tokenization before quant looks identical, but the model's output token ids sequence shows split tokens in the middle of han/kanji clusters. hypothesis: int8 kernel uses a fall-back beam that emits byte-level splits for rare symbol sequences (ruby markers) causing soft-hyphen insertion during detok.

sasha ivanova: action items: (1) run token-level diff between fp16 and int8 outputs (ids and raw strings) on the flagged set; (2) try detok with strip_invisible=true; (3) rerun with int4 emulation to see directionality.

kevin o'neill: i'll queue a kernel-run today to produce id diffs + raw subtoken repr. also will try fast-detok-v1 to check whether v2 introduced the hyphen logic.

cheng li: one more weirdness — bilingual lines (JP with embedded latin year like "2023年") sometimes get hyphenated between digits and 年, producing "202­3年" in outputs. might affect numerics in customer docs.

miki tanaka: not great for invoices. please add a small eval that checks numeric integrity (digits adjacent to CJK ideographs) so we can catch regressions automatically.

raj patel: suggestion: add synthetic tests for ruby/furigana + interpunct combos to the smoke suite and mark them as must-pass for quant rollouts.

cheng li: agreed. i'll open a PR with the testcases and initial bisect artifacts. tagging @sasha for detok change review.

sasha ivanova: ack. also, if bisect points to kernel, we may need a temporary fallback rule: drop soft-hyphen (U+00AD) and ZWSP before exporting shards to customers, while we fix upstream. but prefer root cause fix.

eval-bot: job ci/quick-smoke/aurora-lite-v2/int8/patch-345 started (includes ruby/synthetic tests).

kevin o'neill: i'll monitor. if we can reproduce locally i can iterate on kernel selector and see if using the FP emulation avoids split.

cheng li: thanks all. i'll paste the initial PR + flagged example set here when ready. please react with :eyes: if you want to follow the thread.
